_note: The bought soldier (Sci-Fi Modular Soldier by AC Game Assets; Phase 21, docs/OVERNIGHT_BRIEF_SOLDIER_AND_VERTICAL_CENTRE.md section 3): SpeedKills' only player character when its files are here (npm run paid makes them, locally; they never enter git), the figures of before when they are not. src/game/soldier.ts loads it and builds its materials; src/game/retarget.ts carries the game's clips over to its rig. version is added to every paid file's address, since the game server keeps /models/ for a day and a re-import would otherwise be a day late.
_rename: Its head bone is named head; the game's figures and clips name it Head, and code looks it up by that name (mannequin.ts, outfit.ts, gear.ts, the e2e), so it is renamed as it loads.
_measured: Off soldier.glb at rest by tools/checks/soldier.ts, which fails if the model and these differ: the height from the feet to the top of the head, the pelvis bone's height, the distance between the two upperarm bones, and the ball of the foot's height.
_parts: The model's 18 pieces (triangles), each a skinned mesh on the one skeleton, and the material slot each uses.
_scale: The hit boxes are fixed numbers built for a 1.829 m figure (dummy.ts, H); the soldier stands 1.845 m (measured above), so it is drawn at 1.829 / 1.845, and a headshot lands on its head without moving any hit box.
_tint: How the pack colours it, rebuilt (its Shader Graphs multiply the base colour by a tint wherever a mask is white): the armour by the armour colour (mask R) and the accent (the helmet mask, G); the suit by the suit colour; the head by the skin tone. Colours are sRGB hex; the pack's defaults are the first of each list, converted from its linear values.
_variants: The four the player picks from (the owner: 4 variants, allowing us to change certain things), each a set of the model's pieces and default colours (indexes into the palettes). hide lists the pieces a variant leaves off. The toggles the player has on top of a variant are the helmet, the shoulder plates and the pouches.
